To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optimal policy for the infinite-length video problem is to allocate all available bandwidth to the base layer, while the threshold policy for the finite-length video problem allocates bandwidth to the base and enhancement layers based on a threshold on the available bandwidth.
the optimal dynamic bandwidth allocation policy takes on a simple static form and that the optimal static policy is the same as that for the infinitely-long video case.
the optimal policy is static, that the optimal static policy is simple, and that the optimal policy depends on the relative importance of the base and enhancement layers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and analysis of a dynamic streaming scheme which optimally adapts to the available bandwidth.
the design of optimal prefetching policies for layered video.
the design and evaluation of streaming layered video in the presence of bandwidth fluctuations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best policy is a static policy, and if the base layer is not more important than the enhancement layer, then the best policy is no-prefetch.

for the problem of optimal streaming of layered video, the optimal policy takes one of two forms: either it is static and simple, or it is a threshold policy that switches between two static and simple policies.
prefetching is a good idea and that a static policy is a good choice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the case of layered video, prefetching is beneficial and can be done efficiently by a simple static policy.
for a given video and given random bandwidth process, the optimal policy for prefetching and streaming is a static policy.
for finite-length videos, a static policy can perform well if the base layer is deemed more important.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal policy for streaming layered video is a simple static allocation policy that does not require any knowledge of the bandwidth process.
the optimal policy is surprisingly static, and that prefetching is a powerful tool for improving the quality of streaming video.
, in order to minimize client starvation, the streaming application must be designed to prefetch the entire video.
